title: Contextual load thermograph — mixed context/ingress sweep
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory sweep to capture how tail latency and throughput vary when context length distribution shifts while ingress mix is non-uniform (short requests + occasional long context requests). Want a compact heatmap/thermograph to show safe operating region for Dedicated pools and fallback policies.

Hypothesis:
1) Adding a small fraction (~5%) of long-context (8k tokens) queries will disproportionally increase p95/p99 on higher concurrency due to KV cache pressure and larger KV-read latency.
2) For optimistic batching, effective throughput for short requests will still be good until context > ~2k where scheduling overhead dominates. Quantized variants slightly reduce absolute latency but amplify jitter under burst.

Setup:
- Model: llama-3-8k (native FP16) + opt-quant (4bit) variant for comparison.
- Fleet: single Dedicated pool (A100s), N=8, reserved slots=48 (simulated).
- Client harness: custom harness (bench-runner v0.9) with poisson-modulated arrival, configurable short/long mix.
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99, throughput (tokens/s), kernel time, KV read latency, GPU utilization. 30s warmup + 5min sample per cell.
- Context mixes: short=64 tokens (80% of requests), med=512 (15%), long=4096 (5%). Sweep concurrency: [4,8,16,32,48,64].

Commands (notes to reproduce):
- bench-runner --model llama3-8k --pool=a100-dedicated --mix=short:0.8,med:0.15,long:0.05 --arrival=poisson --concurrency=32 --run=300 --out=csv
- repeat with --model opt-4bit and --concurrency series.

Quick raw summary (representative numbers):
- Concurrency 8 (FP16): p50=45ms, p95=120ms, p99=220ms, tput=9.2k tok/s, GPU util=38%
- Concurrency 32 (FP16): p50=48ms, p95=210ms, p99=620ms, tput=32k tok/s, GPU util=82%
- Concurrency 32 (4-bit): p50=40ms, p95=180ms, p99=840ms, tput=36k tok/s, GPU util=76% (more jitter on p99)
- Concurrency 48 (mixed): p95 jumps to ~350–900ms depending on burst pattern; observed KV-read spikes aligned with long-context completion.

Observations / what stood out:
- p99 sensitivity: small long-request fraction produces long KV read bursts that block batch completion paths and inflate p99 significantly. Suggests need for low-latency isolation (fastlane) or preemptive splitting for long-context.
- 4-bit variant raises throughput but p99 gets worse -> quantization reduces kernel cost but increases scheduling variability (likely more frequent small kernel invocations).
- GPU util correlates poorly with p99 during mixed bursts: util stays high while p99 skyrockets (meaning queuing/serialization rather than compute saturation).
- Short-only baseline shows much smoother tails; mixing contexts is the dominant factor.

Quick thermograph idea (sketch to generate an image later):
- X axis: concurrency; Y axis: fraction of long-context (0% -> 10%); Cell value: p99 (ms) color scale log.
- Overlay contours where p95 > 250ms and where throughput drops >10% from short-only baseline.

Immediate recommendations (for product/ops experiments):
- For Dedicated: allow a fastlane pool (few reserved slots) with context-length-aware routing (detect long-context at ingress and route to separate lane).
- For Hosted fallback: implement adaptive backpressure: when p95 exceeds threshold, route new requests to smaller-context variant or to a cheaper quantized model with strict rate limiting.
- For Optimize: surface quantization tradeoff: show customers a projected p99 increase for mixes with >3% long-context.

Next steps / experiments to run:
1) Repeat with synthetic arrival bursts (sine-modulated lambda) to probe temporal coupling of long-context completions.
2) Increase long-context to 10% and test preemptive KV eviction policy to see if p99 improves.
3) Test with multi-model routing (short->smaller model) to quantify quality vs latency.
4) Trace end-to-end with tracing enabled to capture kernel-level stalls and scheduler contention (need SRE help to enable instrumented builds).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is KV read latency dominated by memcpy or kernel scheduling? (kernel traces needed)
- What is acceptable p99 threshold for PLG vs enterprise SLAs? Need product input.
- How much does prefix caching help if long-context share prefixes vs random contexts?

Notes to self: keep the thermograph as an internal visual for the next infra sync. This doc is messy — extract key numbers into a short slide + one heatmap and share with Kenji + Aisha for prioritization.

Attached/linked artifacts: Linear ticket for routing prototype (INF-876), bench PR with harness changes, confluence page placeholder for generated thermograph images.
